title: Geom Functions
text: Geoms are the geometric objects used to represent data. Every geom function starts with geom_. You can stack multiple geoms in one plot by chaining them with +.

title: Geom Functions
text:
Scatter — geom_point()
library(ggplot2)

# Basic scatter
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point()

# Colour, size, alpha
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8)

# Add regression line
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "tomato")

# Bubble chart — size mapped to data
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, size = hp, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 12))

title: Geom Functions
text:
Lines — geom_line() / geom_path()
# Time-series line chart
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
  geom_line()

# Styled line
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#2d6be4", linewidth = 1)

# Multiple lines by group
ggplot(economics_long, aes(x = date, y = value01, colour = variable)) +
  geom_line()

# Step line (useful for step-wise data)
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
  geom_step()

# geom_path — connects in data order (not sorted by x)
ggplot(economics, aes(x = unemploy/pop, y = psavert)) +
  geom_path(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "Unemployment rate", y = "Personal savings rate")

title: Geom Functions
text:
Bars — geom_bar() / geom_col()
# Count bars (default stat="count")
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar()

# Identity bars (pre-summarised)
df <- data.frame(group = LETTERS[1:4], values = c(5,2,7,2))

ggplot(df, aes(x = group, y = values)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")

# geom_col — shorthand for stat="identity"
ggplot(df, aes(x = group, y = values, fill = group)) +
  geom_col()

# Horizontal with coord_flip
ggplot(df, aes(x = values, y = reorder(group, values))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2d6be4")

# With value labels on top
ggplot(df, aes(x = group, y = values)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = values), vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold")

title: Geom Functions
text:
Histogram — geom_histogram()
# Basic histogram
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10)

# Custom bin width & fill
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 3, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white")

# Density overlay
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = after_stat(density))) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "#c3e7ff", colour = "white", bins = 12) +
  geom_density(colour = "#2d6be4", linewidth = 1)

# Multiple groups
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = 0.6, binwidth = 2, position = "identity")

title: Geom Functions
text:
Density — geom_density()
# Basic density
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_density(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5)

# Multiple groups
cyls <- as.factor(mtcars$cyl)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, fill = cyls)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# 2D density heat map
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_density_2d_filled(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(colour = "white", size = 1.5)

title: Geom Functions
text:
Boxplot — geom_boxplot()
# Basic boxplot
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) +
  geom_boxplot()

# Coloured fill + notches
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_boxplot(notch = TRUE, outlier.colour = "tomato", outlier.size = 2) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# With jittered points overlaid
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "grey90", outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = factor(cyl)), width = 0.15, size = 2, alpha = 0.7)

title: Geom Functions
text:
Violin — geom_violin()
# Basic violin
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6)

# Violin + boxplot combo
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, fill = "white") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(x = "Cylinders", y = "MPG")

title: Geom Functions
text:
Area — geom_area() / geom_ribbon()
# Area chart
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5), colour = "#2d6be4")

# Ribbon — shaded confidence band
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = unemploy - 500, ymax = unemploy + 500),
              fill = "#2d6be4", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = unemploy), colour = "#2d6be4")

# Stacked area chart
library(tidyr)
economics_long |>
  dplyr::filter(variable %in% c("pce","pop")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = value01, fill = variable)) +
  geom_area(alpha = 0.7, position = "stack")

title: Geom Functions
text:
Heatmap — geom_tile() / geom_raster()
# Correlation matrix heatmap
library(tidyr)

cor_df <- as.data.frame(cor(mtcars))
cor_df$var1 <- rownames(cor_df)
cor_long <- pivot_longer(cor_df, -var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "corr")

ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = var1, y = var2, fill = corr)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2d6be4", mid = "white", high = "#e84855", midpoint = 0
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "mtcars Correlation Matrix", fill = "r")

# Calendar heatmap style
ggplot(diamonds, aes(x = cut, y = color, fill = carat)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c()

title: Geom Functions
text:
Smooth trend — geom_smooth()
# Default LOESS smooth
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()

# Linear regression
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "tomato")

# By group
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

# method options: "lm", "glm", "gam", "loess", "rlm"

title: Geom Functions
text:
Jitter — geom_jitter()
# Avoid overplotting in categorical data
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, colour = "steelblue", size = 2, alpha = 0.7)

# geom_jitter is shorthand for geom_point(position = position_jitter())
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15), size = 3, alpha = 0.7)

title: Geom Functions
text:
Error bars — geom_errorbar() / geom_crossbar()
library(dplyr)

# Compute mean and SE per group
summary_df <- mtcars |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarise(mean_mpg = mean(mpg),
            se_mpg   = sd(mpg) / sqrt(n()))

# Error bar plot
ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mean_mpg)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_mpg - se_mpg,
                    ymax = mean_mpg + se_mpg),
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Cylinders", y = "Mean MPG ± SE")

# Point + errorbar
ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mean_mpg)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, colour = "#e84855") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_mpg - se_mpg,
                    ymax = mean_mpg + se_mpg),
                width = 0.2)

title: Geom Functions
text:
Rug marks — geom_rug()
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 0.6)

# Only on x-axis
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_rug(sides = "b")   # "b"=bottom, "l"=left, "t"=top, "r"=right

title: Background & Grid
text:
Plot Margins
library(ggplot2)

# Default margins
ggplot() +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, geom = "density",
                xlim = c(-4, 4), fill = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.1)) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(colour = 1, linewidth = 1))

# Increase margins (in points — default unit)
ggplot() +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, geom = "density",
                xlim = c(-4, 4), fill = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.1)) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(colour = 1, linewidth = 1),
    plot.margin     = margin(
      t = 20,   # Top
      r = 50,   # Right
      b = 40,   # Bottom
      l = 10    # Left
    )
  )

# In centimetres
ggplot() +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, geom = "density",
                xlim = c(-4, 4), fill = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.1)) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(t = 1, r = 1, b = 3, l = 2, unit = "cm")
  )

# Remove margins
ggplot() +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, geom = "density",
                xlim = c(-4, 4), fill = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.1)) +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )






TipRemember TRBL



margin() order: Top, Right, Bottom, Left — the word TRou BLe helps remember it.

title: Coordinate Systems
text:
coord_cartesian() — zoom without clipping
coord_cartesian() zooms into a region without removing data outside the view (unlike xlim() / ylim() which remove data and affect statistical calculations).
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

# Full plot
p

# Zoom in on x: 2–4, y: 15–30  (data outside still used for smooth)
p + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(2, 4), ylim = c(15, 30))

# Compare — xlim() REMOVES data; affects the smooth line
p + xlim(2, 4) + ylim(15, 30)






Importantcoord_cartesian() vs xlim() / ylim()



coord_cartesian() zooms — all data is still used for statistical layers like geom_smooth().
xlim() / ylim() filter — data outside the range is dropped, which can distort stat layers.


# Expand ratio (add padding around data)
p + coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE)          # remove padding
p + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1.5, 5.5),
                    ylim = c(10, 35),
                    expand = FALSE)          # tight zoom, no padding

title: Coordinate Systems
text:
coord_flip() — swap axes
Useful for horizontal bar charts, boxplots, and any chart where switching x/y improves readability.
library(ggplot2)

# Vertical bar chart (default)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar()

# Horizontal bar chart with coord_flip
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar() +
  coord_flip()

# Horizontal sorted bar chart
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = reorder(rownames(mtcars), mpg), y = mpg)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Miles per Gallon",
       title = "Fuel Economy by Car Model")

# Horizontal boxplot
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_flip() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Modern alternative: swap aes() directly (ggplot2 ≥ 3.3)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(y = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar()

title: Coordinate Systems
text:
coord_polar() — pie / radar charts
coord_polar() maps one of the axes to the angle and the other to the radius.
library(ggplot2)

# Pie chart (theta = "y" maps y to angle)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(1), fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(fill = "Cylinders",
       title = "Cylinder distribution in mtcars")

# Coxcomb / Rose chart (theta = "x")
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), fill = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar(width = 1, colour = "white") +
  coord_polar(theta = "x") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Coxcomb chart by cylinder count")

# Radar / spider chart (with line geom)
# For proper radar charts use the fmsb or ggradar packages
# Quick approximation:
ggplot(mtcars[1, ], aes(x = "mpg", y = mpg)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.8) +
  coord_polar() +
  theme_minimal()

title: Coordinate Systems
text:
coord_trans() — transform coordinates
Transforms the visual coordinate space (unlike scale_*_log10() which transforms the data before plotting).
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()

# Log10 Y axis
p + coord_trans(y = "log10")

# Square root on both axes
p + coord_trans(x = "sqrt", y = "sqrt")

# Log on X, reverse Y
p + coord_trans(x = "log10") + scale_y_reverse()

# Compare: scale_y_log10 (transforms data) vs coord_trans (transforms display)
p + scale_y_log10()                    # stat layers use log-transformed data
p + coord_trans(y = "log10")          # stat layers use original data

title: Coordinate Systems
text:
coord_fixed() — fixed aspect ratio
Forces a fixed ratio between x and y units. Default ratio = 1 means one unit on x equals one unit on y.
library(ggplot2)

title: Faceting in ggplot2
text:
Sample data
library(ggplot2)

# Simulate data with 4 groups
set.seed(4)
x      <- runif(500)
y      <- 4 * x^2 + rnorm(length(x), sd = 5)
group  <- ifelse(x < 0.4, "G1",
           ifelse(x < 0.6, "G2",
            ifelse(x < 0.8, "G3", "G4")))
x      <- x + runif(length(x), -0.5, 0.5)
df     <- data.frame(x = x, y = y, group = group)

# All data coloured by group — can get crowded
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point()

title: Faceting in ggplot2
text:
facet_wrap() — one variable

Basic
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group)


Control rows / columns
# Force one row (four panels side by side)
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, nrow = 1)

# Force two columns
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, ncol = 2)


Free axis scales
# All panels independent axes
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, scales = "free")

# Free Y only
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, scales = "free_y")

# Free X only
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, scales = "free_x")


Panel direction
# Default horizontal fill (left→right, then next row)
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, dir = "h")  # default

# Vertical fill (top→bottom, then next column)
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, dir = "v")


Strip (label) position
# Default: top
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, strip.position = "top")    # default

# Bottom strip
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, strip.position = "bottom")

# Left / right
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, strip.position = "left")


Highlight each group (show all data behind)
A powerful technique: draw all data in grey in every panel, then highlight the relevant group on top.
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group)) +
  # All data in grey — remove group from this layer
  geom_point(data = transform(df, group = NULL), colour = "grey85") +
  # Highlighted group on top
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, strip.position = "bottom")

title: Faceting in ggplot2
text:
facet_grid() — two variables
# Simulate second grouping variable
set.seed(4)
x      <- runif(500)
y      <- 4 * x^2 + rnorm(length(x), sd = 5)
group1 <- ifelse(x < 0.4, "G1", ifelse(x < 0.6, "G2",
           ifelse(x < 0.8, "G3", "G4")))
group2 <- ifelse(y < 0.5, "A", "B")
x      <- x + runif(length(x), -0.5, 0.5)
df2    <- data.frame(x = x, y = y, group1 = group1, group2 = group2)

Basic formula syntax
# group1 ~ group2 → group1 in rows, group2 in columns
ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group1)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(group1 ~ group2)


vars() syntax (modern)
ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group1)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(group1), cols = vars(group2))


One direction only
# Only columns (rows free)
ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ group2)

# Only rows (cols free)
ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(group1 ~ .)


Free scales
ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group1)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(group1 ~ group2, scales = "free")

# Free only Y
ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group1)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(group1 ~ group2, scales = "free_y")

ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = group1)) +
  geom_point(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(group1 ~ group2,
             scales = "free",
             space  = "free")   # "free", "free_x", "free_y"

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +

    name   = "Cylinders"

text:
General annotations — annotate()
annotate() is a versatile function for adding shapes, text, and lines without a data frame.

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()

# Text
p + annotate("text", x = 4.5, y = 30,
             label = "Annotation text",
             colour = "tomato", size = 5, fontface = "bold")

# Rectangle (shaded region)
p + annotate("rect",
             xmin = 1.5, xmax = 2.5,
             ymin = 25,  ymax = 35,
             alpha = 0.15, fill = "steelblue")

# Segment
p + annotate("segment",
             x = 2, y = 20,
             xend = 3, yend = 25,
             colour = "red", linewidth = 1,
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3,"cm")))

# Point
p + annotate("point", x = 3.5, y = 20,
             colour = "red", size = 5, shape = 18)

# Label box
p + annotate("label",
             x = 4, y = 32,
             label = "Outlier zone",
             fill = "#fff3cd", colour = "darkorange")

title: Annotations, Lines & Arrows
text:
Reference lines

Vertical lines — geom_vline()
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), y = rnorm(100))

# Single vertical line
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = 2)

# Multiple vertical lines
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 0, 1),
             linetype    = 1,
             colour      = 2:4,
             linewidth   = 0.8)

# Vertical line at the mean
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 12, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(mtcars$mpg),
             colour = "tomato", linetype = 2, linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = mean(mtcars$mpg) + 1.5, y = 7,
           label = paste0("Mean = ", round(mean(mtcars$mpg), 1)),
           colour = "tomato", hjust = 0)


Horizontal lines — geom_hline()
# Single horizontal line
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = 2)

# Multiple horizontal lines
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 0, 1),
             linetype   = 3,
             colour     = 4,
             linewidth  = 1)


Diagonal lines — geom_abline()
# y = x line (identity line)
ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1,
              colour = "tomato", linetype = 2)

# Custom regression line
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = coef(model)[1],
              slope     = coef(model)[2],
              colour    = "steelblue", linewidth = 1)

title: Titles, Labels & Text Styling
text:
Title

Using ggtitle()
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  ggtitle("US Unemployment Over Time")


Using labs()
ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "US Unemployment Over Time")


Title position
Default: aligned to the panel (plot data area).
Set "plot" to align to the full figure including margins.
ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title = "Aligned to full plot width") +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot")   # "panel" | "plot"

Subtitle

  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +

          subtitle = "Subtitle of the plot")

Caption

  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(title   = "US Unemployment",
       caption = "Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics")

# Move caption to left
ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(caption = "Source: BLS") +
  theme(plot.caption.position = "plot",
        plot.caption           = element_text(hjust = 0))  # 0=left, 1=right

  labs(title = "US Unemployment", tag = "Fig. 1")

ggplot(economics, aes(date, unemploy)) +
  geom_area(fill = rgb(0, 0.5, 1, alpha = 0.5)) +
  labs(tag = "A") +
  theme(plot.tag.position = "bottomright")

Legend position

ggplot(df, aes(x = x, fill = group)) +

  theme(legend.position = "top")

  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +

Setting a global theme
Use theme_set() to apply a theme to all subsequent plots in your session:
library(ggplot2)

# Save current theme and set a new one
old <- theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))

# Now ALL plots use theme_minimal

title: Themes & Styling
text:
Custom theme with theme()
Build your own reusable theme:
library(ggplot2)

my_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    # Titles
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16,
                                   colour = "#0e0f14", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = "#6b6760", size = 12,
                                   margin = margin(b = 12)),
    plot.caption    = element_text(colour = "#aaaaaa", size = 9, hjust = 1),

    # Axes
    axis.title      = element_text(size = 11, colour = "#3d3e47"),
    axis.text       = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#6b6760"),
    axis.line       = element_line(colour = "#d8d2c8"),

    # Grid
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#ede8df", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#faf8f4", colour = NA),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff", colour = NA),

    # Legend
    legend.position  = "top",
    legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 10),

    # Facet strips
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),

    # Margins
    plot.margin      = margin(16, 16, 16, 16)
  )

# Apply to any plot
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#e84855","#2d6be4","#12a36a")) +
  labs(title = "Custom Theme", colour = "Cylinders") +
  my_theme

title: Bar Charts (5 Examples)
text:
Example 2 — ggplot2 basic bar chart
library(ggplot2)

Vertical (default)
# stat = "identity" — use y values as-is
ggplot(df1, aes(x = group, y = values)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")

# geom_col() is shorthand for geom_bar(stat = "identity")
ggplot(df1, aes(x = group, y = values)) +
  geom_col()


Horizontal with coord_flip()
ggplot(df1, aes(x = group, y = values)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip()


Sorted horizontal bars
ggplot(df1, aes(x = values, y = reorder(group, values))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Values", y = "Group")


With colours and legend
ggplot(df1, aes(x = group, y = values, fill = group)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#e84855","#2d6be4","#12a36a","#d4a017")) +
  theme_minimal()


With value labels
ggplot(df1, aes(x = group, y = values, fill = group)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = values), vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


stat = “count” (count rows, no y mapping needed)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_x_discrete(name = "Number of Cylinders") +
  labs(y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

title: Bar Charts (5 Examples)
text:
Example 3 — Stacked bar chart
Stacked bars show how subgroups contribute to a total. Map fill to the subgroup variable.
ggplot(df2, aes(x = maingroup, y = values, fill = subgroup)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")

Styled stacked chart
ggplot(df2, aes(x = maingroup, y = values, fill = subgroup)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("a" = "#2d6be4", "b" = "#e84855")) +
  geom_text(aes(label = values),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  labs(title = "Stacked Bar Chart",
       x = "Group", y = "Values", fill = "Subgroup") +
  theme_minimal()

title: Bar Charts (5 Examples)
text:
Example 4 — 100% stacked (proportional)
Scale all bars to the same height to compare proportions across groups.

Scaled to 1.0
ggplot(df2, aes(x = maingroup, y = values, fill = subgroup)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill")
# Y axis shows 0.00 – 1.00


Scaled to 100%
library(scales)

ggplot(df2, aes(x = maingroup, y = values, fill = subgroup)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(y = "Percentage") +
  theme_minimal()


With percentage labels inside bars
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

df2_pct <- df2 |>
  group_by(maingroup) |>
  mutate(pct = values / sum(values))

ggplot(df2_pct, aes(x = maingroup, y = values, fill = subgroup)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(pct, accuracy = 1)),
            position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5),
            colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("a" = "#2d6be4", "b" = "#e84855")) +
  labs(title = "100% Stacked Bar Chart", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal()

title: Bar Charts (5 Examples)
text:
Example 5 — Grouped (dodged) bar chart
Grouped bars place subgroups side by side. Use position = "dodge".
ggplot(df2, aes(x = maingroup, y = values, fill = subgroup)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge")

Fine-tune gap between bars
ggplot(df2, aes(x = maingroup, y = values, fill = subgroup)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",
           position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
           width    = 0.7)


Full styled grouped chart with value labels
ggplot(df2, aes(x = maingroup, y = values, fill = subgroup)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity",

title: Combining Plots
text:
patchwork
install.packages("patchwork")
library(patchwork)

Basic operators
# + (or |) — side by side
p1 + p2
p1 | p2

# / — stacked (vertical)
p1 / p2

# 4 plots in auto-layout
p1 + p2 + p3 + p4

# Complex nesting
(p1 | p2) / p3           # two on top, one wide at bottom
p1 | (p2 / p3)            # one at left, two stacked at right
p1 + ((p2 | p3) / p4)     # nested 3-panel right side


plot_layout() — control layout
# Set number of columns
p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3)

# Relative widths and heights
p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 +
  plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1), heights = c(1, 2))

# Custom design string
# 1,2,3,4 = plot numbers; # = empty space
p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 +
  plot_layout(design = "
    111
    2#3
    443
  ")


wrap_plots() — for lists of plots
# When you don't know the number of plots at coding time
wrap_plots(p1, p2, p3, p4,
           ncol    = 2,
           nrow    = 2,
           widths  = c(1, 0.5),
           heights = c(0.5, 1))

# From a list (e.g. from lapply)
plot_list <- list(p1, p2, p3, p4)
wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 2)


plot_spacer() — add empty gaps
p1 + plot_spacer() + p3         # p1 | gap | p3

# Multi-row with spacers
(p1 + plot_spacer() + p2) /
(p3 + p4 + plot_spacer())


plot_annotation() — overall title & panel labels
# Overall title, subtitle, caption
p1 + ((p2 | p3) / p4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "Combined plot title",
    subtitle = "A subtitle for the whole figure",
    caption  = "Source: mtcars dataset"
  )

# Automatic panel labels
p1 + p2 +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")    # A, B, C…

p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "1")    # 1, 2, 3, 4

# Labels with prefix
p1 + p2 +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A",
                  tag_prefix = "Fig. ")   # Fig. A, Fig. B

# Roman numerals
p1 + p2 +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "i")    # i, ii, iii…


& operator — apply to all panels
# Set same theme for all plots at once
p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 & theme_minimal()

# Combined with annotation
(p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 & theme_minimal()) +
  plot_annotation(title = "All with theme_minimal")


Add new layers to a patchwork
# Adds to the LAST plot in the patchwork
p2 + p1 + geom_jitter(colour = "tomato")

# Access specific plot by index
patch <- p2 + p1
patch[[1]] <- patch[[1]] + theme_bw()
patch


Mix ggplot2 with base R plots
old_par <- par()
par(mar = c(0, 2, 0, 0), bg = NA)
p1 + wrap_elements(panel = ~ plot(1:10))
par(old_par)


Add a table (with gridExtra)
library(gridExtra)

tab <- t(round(quantile(mtcars$mpg), 2))
p1 / tableGrob(tab)


Add text annotations
library(grid)

p1 + textGrob("Text at the right")
wrap_elements(textGrob("Text at the left")) + p1

Data Frames
A data frame is R’s tabular data structure — like a spreadsheet. Each column is a vector; all columns have equal length.
Syntax: df[row, column] — first argument = row, second = column.
# Create a data frame
data.frame(
  x = 1:7,
  y = c("Sun","Mon","Tue","Wed","Thurs","Fri","Sat")
) -> df
df

# Access columns
df[ , 2]      # all rows, column 2
df$x          # column x by name (returns vector)
df[2,  ]      # all columns of row 2
df[1:3, 1]    # rows 1–3, column 1

# Useful info
nrow(df)      # number of rows
ncol(df)      # number of columns
dim(df)       # c(rows, cols)
str(df)       # structure overview
head(df)      # first 6 rows
tail(df)      # last 6 rows
summary(df)   # descriptive statistics

colnames(df)  # same as names

library(dplyr)

title: ggplot2 — Introduction & Grammar of Graphics
text:
ggplot2 is a powerful, open-source data visualization library for R developed by Hadley Wickham. It is based on the Grammar of Graphics — a systematic framework for describing any statistical graphic as a combination of layers.
One of ggplot2’s defining strengths is layered plot construction: start with data, map aesthetics, add geometric objects, then refine with scales, facets, and themes — each + call adds a new layer.
install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)

text:
Aesthetics (aes)
The aes() function maps data variables to visual properties. There are two kinds:

Mapped (inside aes()) — value varies by data
Fixed (outside aes()) — constant for all data points

# MAPPED — colour changes per group
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point()

# FIXED — all points are steelblue, size 3
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 3, alpha = 0.7)

# BOTH — shape mapped to data, colour fixed
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt, shape = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(colour = "tomato", size = 3)

section: Building a Plot Step by Step
text:
Building a Plot Step by Step
library(ggplot2)

# Step 1: data + aesthetics
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg))

# Step 2: add geometry
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point()

# Step 3: map colour to a third variable
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3)

# Step 4: add a smooth trend line
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)

# Step 5: labels
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Weight vs MPG", colour = "Cylinders",
       x = "Weight (1,000 lbs)", y = "Miles per Gallon")

# Step 6: theme
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Weight vs MPG", colour = "Cylinders",
       x = "Weight (1,000 lbs)", y = "Miles per Gallon") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

text:
Scales
Scales control how data values map to visual properties.
# Axis limits
scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 50), breaks = seq(0, 50, by = 10))
scale_y_log10()
scale_x_date(date_labels = "%Y-%m")
scale_x_reverse()

# Colour & fill — continuous
scale_colour_gradient(low = "white", high = "darkred")
scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0)

# Colour & fill — discrete
scale_colour_manual(values = c("#e84855", "#2d6be4", "#12a36a"))
scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")
scale_colour_viridis_d()          # colorblind-friendly

# Axis labels
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format())
scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)
scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar)

title: ggplot2 — Introduction & Grammar of Graphics
text:
Faceting
Faceting splits data into multiple sub-panels.
library(ggplot2)

# facet_wrap — one variable
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ gear)

# Custom rows / columns
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ cyl, nrow = 1)

# Free scales per panel
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ cyl, scales = "free")

# facet_grid — two variables
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(am ~ cyl)            # rows ~ columns

# Only column facets
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(. ~ cyl)

text:
Key ggplot2 Functions
# Labels
labs(title = , subtitle = , caption = , x = , y = , colour = , fill = , tag = )
ggtitle("Title", subtitle = "Subtitle")
xlab("X axis")  ;  ylab("Y axis")

# Coordinates
coord_flip()                    # swap x and y
coord_polar(theta = "y")        # pie / radar charts
coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0,5))  # zoom without dropping data
coord_fixed()                   # equal unit lengths on both axes

# Annotations
annotate("text",  x = 2, y = 3, label = "Note")
annotate("rect",  xmin = 1, xmax = 2, ymin = 0, ymax = 5, alpha = 0.1)
annotate("segment", x = 1, y = 1, xend = 3, yend = 3, arrow = arrow())

# Theme shortcuts
theme_grey()       # default
theme_bw()         # black & white
theme_minimal()    # no background
theme_classic()    # axes only, no grid
theme_dark()       # dark panel
theme_void()       # blank canvas

# Set global theme
old <- theme_set(theme_minimal())
theme_set(old)     # restore

# Save
ggsave("plot.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)

text:
The theme() Function
The theme() function overrides any non-data visual element:
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(
    # Text elements
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 12, colour = "grey50"),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 1),
    axis.title        = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text         = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x       = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),

    # Panel
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "#f0f4f8"),
    panel.grid.major  = element_line(colour = "#dce3ec", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    panel.border      = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA),

    # Legend
    legend.position   = "top",
    legend.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),

    # Margins
    plot.margin       = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20)
  )
